reasoning: The claim that humans only use 10% of their brain capacity is a widely debunked neuro myth. According to neuroscientists and research institutes like the MIT McGovern Institute, brain imaging technologies such as fMRI and PET scans demonstrate that virtually all parts of the brain are active throughout the day, even during sleep and simple tasks. Furthermore, damage to almost any area of the brain can cause severe functional impairment, and unused neural tissue naturally degenerates or atrophies over time, confirming that no large portion of the brain lies dormant or untapped.
